chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadhr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Imran ibn Miytham, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A man recited for the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, they do not call you liar, but the wrongdoers reject the signs of Allah.'

He (the Imam) said: 'Yes, by Allah, they rejected him with a most severe rejection, but it (the word in the verse) is softened (pronounced without Shadda): 'La yukadhdhibunaka' (they do not call you a liar), meaning: they will not come with a falsehood by which to negate your truth.'

key_terms.لَا يُكَذِّبُونَكَ: they do not call you a liar (softened reading)
key_terms.يَجْحَدُونَ: to reject or deny (specifically regarding signs)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the softened reading (qira'a) of 'yukadhdhibunaka' in Surah Yunus according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explains the grammatical nuance of the Quranic verse Surah Yunus (10:82), where the word 'yukadhdhibunaka' is read without a shadda (softened). He clarifies that while the disbelievers did not literally call the Prophet a liar in the sense of denying his message entirely, they rejected him with severe rejection, and the softened reading implies they did not bring a falsehood that could completely invalidate his truth.

en.ammaar-muslim: [5/1570] al-Kafi: Muhammad b. Yahya from Ahmad b. Muhammad from al-Husayn b. Sa’id from al-Nadhr b. Suwayd from Muhammad b. Abi Hamza from Ya’qub b. Shuayb from Imran b. Miytham from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام who said:
A man recited for the Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام - ‘Fa Innahum La Yukadhdhibunaka wa Lakinna l-Dhalimina bi Ayati-llahi Yajhadun’

so he (i.e. the Imam) said: Indeed by Allah - they rejected him (i.e. the prophet) a most severe rejection, but it (the word in the verse) is softened (i.e. pronounced without Shadda) ‘La Yukdhibunaka’, (that is) they will not come with a falsehood by which to negate your truth (i.e. render it false)
